why: npm audit has never passed here and cannot be made to: node-forge 1.4.0 is the newest published version and the advisory lists no patched version. A permanently red CI step teaches everyone to ignore the exit code, including for genuinely new advisories, so known ones are recorded here and reported every run instead. Any NEW high/critical advisory still fails the build.

advisories.title: node-forge RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification accepts extra nested DigestAlgorithm elements
advisories.patchedVersions: none published (node-forge 1.4.0 is the newest release)
advisories.why: Build tooling, not shipped. @expo/cli uses node-forge to verify iOS code-signing certificates during a local Expo build. The deployed artefact is apps/website/dist/index.html, a self-contained static file with no dependency on expo; grepping the built output for expo or forge returns nothing. The flaw is RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature forgery against low-exponent keys, and we verify only certificates we generated ourselves, so there is no attacker-controlled input. Revisit when node-forge ships a patch (there is none published as of 2 Oct 2026), or if @expo/cli ever verifies untrusted signatures.
